newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DISNEY TARGETS AFRICA THROUGH S.AFRICAN PRESENCE.
newsitem.headline: DISNEY TARGETS AFRICA THROUGH S.AFRICAN PRESENCE.

text.p: The Walt Disney Company on Tuesday launched a South African subsidiary to consolidate its 300 million rand-a-year retail business and explore avenues into the rest of Africa.
"The whole idea is to use South Africa as a base to go into the rest of Africa," said Pierre Sissmann, president of Disney Consumer Products, Europe, Middle East and Africa.
"We don't know Africa. We don't know what the potential is. We have a lot to learn and we are here to do that," he said in an interview.
Sissmann said the registration of Disney Enterprises Southern Africa was the international entertainment and franchise group's first foothold in Africa.
"We could have started in Francophone Africa, Senegal, and worked our way down, but we decided we would much rather start in South Africa and work our way north," he said.
Ray Botha, managing director of the South African subsidiary, said Disney products, mainly toys and textiles, retailed for around 300 million rand per year in South Africa.
Disney has been marketing in South Africa through licensees for more than 25 years, but has not previously had a registered presence in the country.

Botha, a South African, said about 60 percent of the merchandise was made under licence in South Africa with exports, mainly to the Middle East, up from zero to "several hundred thousands rand a year" in the past 18 months.
He said his local company would be looking for creative, production and marketing partnerships with South African companies, both for the domestic market and for export.
Sissmann said Disney would be on the look-out for unique cultural and marketing ideas that could be taken from South Africa into new markets.
He said the company would offer management support and the Disney licence, but did not expect heavy capital investment in its South African partnerships.
